thread:
nikita: Quick thread — proposing an "opaque registry proxy" approach for air-gapped packaging + operator coordination. Goal: operator only talks to a local HTTPS proxy that exposes a stable registry-like API; proxy slices sealed bundles from removable media or an internal mirror and enforces activation tokens and backpressure. Summary in 2 bullets:

nikita: - decouple operator from transport (usb/rsync/mirror)
nikita: - proxy provides resume tokens, chunked fetch, and signer verification locally :lock:

matt: Can you sketch the handshake flow? I'm picturing a lot of edge cases for partial upgrades. :thinking:

nikita: Sure, rough sequence:```
1) admin drops seed bundle on media (or mirror sync)
2) proxy indexes bundle, exposes /v2/registry-like endpoints
3) operator calls proxy /licenses/activate -> proxy returns activation token + blob manifest
4) operator streams blobs in chunked order, ack per-chunk
5) proxy maintains resume token and idempotency markers
6) operator validates signatures before apply, signals completion
```

jess: Two immediate concerns: signature rotation + KMS escrow for enterprise customers. If customer rotates signing key between mirror creation and operator apply, we need an escrow or cross-signed timeline. Also, what about verifying provenance offline?

nikita: Agreed. Proposal: embed a "signing-epoch" header in manifests and ship a compact escrow envelope with each bundle that includes cross-sigs for N previous epochs. We keep the verifier simple: check current keyset OR valid cross-sig chain. If neither -> operator refuses unless admin override.

sam: What about payload size and memory pressure on proxies? Some customers will have multi-GB model shards. Proxy can't load entire model into RAM.

nikita: Proxy will expose range/byte endpoints and support streaming with small memory window. We should also support chunk-idempotency so operator can retry chunks without reapplying. Implementation note: use content-addressed chunks and a local disk-backed index (LMDB or sqlite).

matt: Operator UX question: how does the operator surface partial progress and safe rollback? We need deterministic activation windows so controllers don't flip-flop during partial apply.

nikita: Idea: activation window state machine with phases: PREPARE -> STREAMING -> STAGED -> ACTIVATION -> COMMIT. Operator treats STAGED as safe fallback point (can abort to previous commit). The proxy can hold a tombstone key for in-flight activations that operator queries to decide whether to continue.

jess: Also, audit logs. Must capture per-chunk hash, signer id, timestamp, and verifier outcome. Customers will want this for compliance. Keep logs local + optional upload to customer SIEM when network available.

ops-bot: snapshot created: snapshot-1738009123-proxy-idea (links: https://storage.internal/snapshots/1738009123) :robot_face:

sam: Failure modes: media gets corrupted mid-stream. Resume token + chunk checksums should allow restart. But we need operator guidance for partial decryption states (especially for encrypted model shards).

nikita: For encrypted shards: decrypt on-the-fly with per-chunk IVs and a streaming KMS interface. If decryption fails mid-stream, operator reports and proxy marks activation as FAILED with retry window. Admin must re-provision media or mirror.

matt: One more: compatibility with existing airgap playbooks (seed + delta). Can the proxy support both full-seed and incremental deltas?

nikita: Yes — manifest format supports "delta" sections: base pointers + delta ops. Proxy can serve either full blobs or patch deltas. Operator decides prefer-delta or full based on local heuristics (disk, time, rollback risk).

jess: Security checklist we should include in RFC: signer epoch cross-sigs, KMS escrow procedure, HSM integration notes, per-chunk attestations, offline audit export, admin override policy, and operator-safe-abort semantics.

sam: We should prototype a tiny proxy that serves a small model from a USB image and a controller that resumes after simulated bitflip. Can do PoC in next sprint.

nikita: Agreed. Next steps: I'll write RFC draft with handshake diagrams, manifest schema, state machine, and failure playbook. Call out operator API changes and disk-backed proxy index.

matt: Awesome. Add a short migration section for onprem customers currently using seed-only flows. Also include a compatibility shim for older operator versions.

jess: :thumbsup: Add compliance examples (PCI / FedRAMP) for audit export.

nikita: Will do. Tagging for follow-up: @matt @jess @sam. Thanks all — filing RFC next.
